chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Yūnus, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Sinān, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a wound: how should its possessor deal with it? He said: “He washes what is around it.”

key_terms.الْجُرْحِ: a wound or injury on the body
key_terms.صَاحِبُهُ: the person who has the wound
key_terms.مَا حَوْلَهُ: what is around it, meaning the surrounding area
key_terms.يَصْنَعُ: acts or proceeds; how one should deal with the matter

ai.seo_question: How should a person perform wudu (ablution) when there is a wound on the body?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning ritual purification when a person has a wound. It indicates that in wudu (ablution), the area surrounding the wound should be washed, showing practical accommodation in cases of bodily injury.
